instance.finding_key: packages/sheets/src/store/cell-index.ts::new public `cellindex.bounds()` has no unit test; it is only covered indirectly through memstore calculation tests, so its own edge cases (data not starting at a1, becoming empty after removals, independent row/col minima) are unverified.

finding.summary: New public `CellIndex.bounds()` has no unit test; it is only covered indirectly through MemStore calculation tests, so its own edge cases (data not starting at A1, becoming empty after removals, independent row/col minima) are unverified.
finding.evidence: packages/sheets/src/store/cell-index.ts:128-149 adds `bounds()`. packages/sheets/test/store/cell-index.test.ts (read in full, 201 lines) is untouched by the diff and contains no `bounds` reference — I grepped the whole test tree for `bounds` and got no hit in that file. E.g. `bounds()` returning `undefined` after `remove()` empties the index, or a sheet whose data starts at C5, is never asserted anywhere.

decision.reason: The factual premise is correct (bounds() is new and cell-index.test.ts is untouched), but the new behavior is NOT untested: it is covered by 8 new, unmocked integration tests whose expected values are directly derived from bounds()' output. calculate() routes through sheet.getUsedBounds() -> MemStore.getUsedBounds() -> cellIndex.bounds(), and the new tests use a real Sheet + real MemStore + real CellIndex. Assertions like =SUM(1:3) -> '360' (requires maxC=2), =COUNT(A:B) -> '5' (requires maxR=3), and 'picks up a newly added cell beyond the prior data extent' (A10 added -> '65', requires bounds() to grow with the index) would all fail if bounds()' min/max computation broke. The specific uncovered corners named by the finding are narrow: the truly-empty-index undefined path has an adjacent empty-sheet test, and the independent row/col MINIMA the finding worries about are never consumed downstream since resolveRange destructures only the max endpoint (`const [, max] = bounds;`). Under this lens's rubric that is 'coverage could be broader' = minor, and the rubric explicitly says not to flag 'add more tests' as blocking when the core behavior is tested. Note: the repo working tree was empty, so I verified entirely against diff.patch, which is authoritative for this change and contains the full text of both the added bounds() method and every added test.
